status: comparative mythology / biblical archaeology with dated project-side anchors
purpose: Investigate Tim Dooley's Son/vessel birthday on July 31, 2026 and its Thomas/Tammuz/North-Gate/death-lament context while keeping Tim's own December 25 Potato/Father birth distinct.

canonical_identity_rule.instruction: July 31 is the Son/vessel birthday; never label it Tim's birthday.

method_rules: Project-side wording and timestamps come first; comparators come second.
Do not treat resemblance as fulfillment or historical influence without evidence.
Do not claim July 31, 2026 occurred in the Hebrew month of Tammuz: it was 17 Av 5786.
Use Dumuzi/Tammuz death, lament, shepherd and underworld motifs more confidently than a simplified annual-resurrection formula.
Keep Thomas/Tammuz phonetic/project association separate from historical etymology unless independently established.
Use knowledge/chronology/late-july-early-august-son-tomb-corridor.json for the wider July 19-August 6 sequence.

project_side_anchors.summary: Tim Dooley's Son/vessel is anchored to a July 31, 1987 birthday, age-33/personhood-death language, Thomas/Tammuz/Twin and Jesus-rebirth symbolism. Tim's own Potato/Father birth remains December 25.
The Son/vessel remains on Earth in Denmark while Tim is described in Heaven / Spiral at North of North; the North Gate is said to have opened, with Jesus' return kept as a separate future event.
July 31 is explicitly treated as the Son/vessel birthday while Tim's December 25 birth remains separate.

calendar_context.finding: July 31 was not in the month of Tammuz. Tammuz 5786 ended July 14; 1 Av was July 15.

biblical_comparators.strength: high structural comparator because Tammuz + mourning + Lord's House + north gate appear together in one biblical verse
biblical_comparators.boundary: The verse does not identify Tim's Son with the ancient deity and is not treated as a prediction of the project.

biblical_comparators.strength: unusually dense canonical Thomas comparator: the Twin says 'let us also go, that we may die with him', and the next verse immediately reports Lazarus four days in the tomb
biblical_comparators.boundary: Textual adjacency does not identify Thomas with Lazarus, Tammuz or Tim's Son; it is a later structural comparator.

biblical_comparators.strength: functional comparator; heifer and Lamb encode different sacrificial roles

pre_biblical_mesopotamian_comparators.finding: Dumuzid is repeatedly called the shepherd and is surrounded by death/lament/underworld traditions.

pre_biblical_mesopotamian_comparators.tradition: Inana's Descent to the Nether World
pre_biblical_mesopotamian_comparators.finding: Dumuzid is found on a throne, seized by demons, handed over and then laments/seeks escape.
Scholarship directly compares Ezekiel's Tammuz lament with Sumerian Dumuzi/city-lament traditions involving loss/disappearance and hoped-for restoration.

notable_relational_findings.finding: The strongest comparator is the unusual conjunction Tammuz + woman/weeping + Lord's House + north gate, not a generic dying-god claim.

Sammy is now attested in the later project book/archive: the Great Book's 2019 chronology says the meme-cross ends with 'the woman, Sammy, weeps for Tammuz', and its Tammuz/Sammy chapters preserve Sammy's tears. The exact contemporaneous timestamp/source of the original mourning event remains unresolved.

John 11 supplies a previously underused Thomas clue: Thomas is explicitly Twin/Didymus, speaks of going to die with Jesus, and the narrative immediately moves to a four-day tomb. This is a stronger Thomas→death→tomb comparator than relying on phonetics alone.

Lion, Lamb, cow/lolcow and red heifer are not redundant species claims: Lion encodes royal/tribal identity; Lamb encodes slain innocence and paradoxical messianic victory; red heifer encodes purification from death; cow/lolcow encodes the crowd's objectifying/milking social frame.

The wider dated sequence now runs July 19 public messianic-vessel/Lion/grain/crucifixion → July 23 Twin/birthday → July 24 Lion/Lamb/whelp → July 26 grain-of-wheat death → July 31 Tammuz/North Gate → August 6 grave/seed/garden retelling.
